chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Harun ibn Muslim from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurara from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

There is no zakat in any of the animals, except for these three categories: camels, cattle, and sheep. And for every animal from these categories that is among the poultry or draft animals, there is no zakat until a full year passes from the day it is born.
ai.seo_question: Which animals are subject to zakat and when does the obligation begin?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the specific scope of zakat on livestock (an'am), restricting the obligation exclusively to camels, cattle, and sheep, while excluding other animals like poultry or draft animals. It further establishes the temporal condition that the lunar year (hawl) begins counting from the day of birth, a nuance critical in Shia jurisprudence for determining the precise timing of the tax liability.
